steps.name: Reporter A
steps.text: Hurry! All the headlines will be the Vice President's visit to Rhine tomorrow. The editor-in-chief will have our heads if we don't get a good photo.

steps.name: Reporter B
steps.text: Wait, I can't find my press pass...

steps.name: Reporter A
steps.text: What? You can't go in without it!

steps.name: Reporter B
steps.text: Go find a good spot! I'll look for it.

steps.name: Rhine Staff A
steps.text: So many people...

steps.name: Rhine Staff A
steps.text: I couldn't even get to the café downstairs for breakfast.

steps.name: Rhine Staff B
steps.text: A public visit by the Vice President, broadcasted live. Every newspaper is here. It's a wonder they didn't completely block the roads.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: You see it, Rosmontis?

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: First the factory, then Rhine Lab. Trimounts likes to block off a place when something happens.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Rhine Lab is different from the factory, isn't it? They blocked off some of the key roads leading in. Probably out of security concerns for the Vice President's convoy.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Which causes other streets to fill up.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Did they think people wouldn't see if they blocked it off? That's dumb.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: ...Mm-hm.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Doctor, what are you looking at?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Sunny all day long! The hotel TV had the weather report on when were leaving. Guess you didn't see it.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Anyway, it's not the rainy season yet.
Another sunny day.

The urban planning of Trimounts is intricate, the gaps between the staggered skyscrapers allowing sunlight to pass through, for the sun to paint each street with warm light evenly in these early days of winter.
You look up to see a dark cloud in the distance, floating nonchalantly in the sky. The wind is blowing toward the cloud, and it looks to be moving away from the city.
But it never disappears.
You also see the busy streets, the parked cars, a flash of light up high in the distance, and well-disguised 'passersby'...
You keep a poker face while urging the two girls on.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Did you find something, Doctor?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Don't worry, Doctor, we'll protect you.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I know, I know. You've said it a dozen times before we left.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I promised to listen to you, and I keep my promises.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I think we're there.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}. We meet again.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: As usual, I'm the one waiting.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ah, well, I got here before you. I got myself ready as soon as your message came in.

options: This is your company, after all...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Well, this is what you asked for... plans for the Rhine Lab building, and visitor's passes for you and your young assistants.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I called in a few favors to get you clearance to most of the building and data. Today only.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: There are lots of hidden spaces in the building, both above and below ground. My tip is to have someone focus on the underground.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I have to accompany Mr. Vice President on his Rhine tour, of course.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Kristen's not here, and we're missing a few section heads. Can't have anyone else calling out.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'll give you a big, personal thank you when we're all done.

options: You may be on your own, Ifrit.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I read your resignation letter, Bieber. Why so sudden?

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: I'm sorry, Director Jara.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: I discovered something yesterday.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: Energy's wing has 38 ceiling lamps and 21 vents.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: The carpet beneath our feet looks the same at first glance, but a closer look reveals that there are actually three versions, subtly different in pattern and fringes.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I didn't know you were planning to go into interior design, Bieber.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: You would've done the same if all the projects you're involved in are up in the air, and the only work you have to do each day is to re-read the report that you wrote the day before.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I understand. It's hard work, keeping your guys calm while pretending that everything is business as usual.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: I could live with hard work, Director.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: The labs have always been relatively independent of one another, and research is modular. Everybody goes about their own business, even if something happens to Site 359, even if Ferdinand quits unexpectedly.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: At the lower levels, people don't know much and believe this is no different from any number of 'research accidents' that have happened before, the kind that every tech company deals with every now and then.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: But I know this one is different...

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: Control has virtually vanished without a trace, and Ferdinand suddenly resigned. Every day is like sitting on a fire. There's been no formal change of leadership in Energy, no one to tell me what happened, or what I should do.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: Now the Vice President is touring Rhine. It makes my stomach seize up when I walk into the lab and see the excitement in everybody's eyes.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: So you talked to Volvort Kochinski's headhunter... Sonya, right?

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: I... yes.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I'm not reprimanding you, Bieber.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Your position at Rhine Lab allows you to see more than the average employee, but not the full picture. It's normal to feel anxious.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: The responsibility falls on me. I asked you to keep things calm in the Energy Section, but neglected your own emotional needs.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: I-It's not your fault. Just weakness on my part...

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Why do you think the Vice President is making this sudden visit?

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: I... I don't know. But he'll find out that we're...

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: The press conference that he held a few days ago has to do with us.

steps.name: Energy Section Researcher
steps.text: ...Really?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: That's all I can tell you for now.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: How about this? Take one month off. Paid leave. Maybe it'll be enough for you to clear your head and return to your post.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: If you still insist on resigning after that, I won't stop you.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Rhine Lab grew from a single lab to ten sections, running more than a hundred large-scale projects simultaneously. It has seen bigger storms.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: It has survived them all.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Just give it a little thought.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Sorry for the trouble, Sonya.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: The staff need a way to vent in times like this.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Bieber should be the last one. If he's okay, the Energy Section is okay for now.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Yeah, catch you for lunch or dinner one of these days. Give Tin Man my thanks.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: How many does that make this week?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Not your problem.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Just don't send them to Business if you're reassigning them. I don't need flighty idiots like that.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: They're cornerstones of this company, Justin, just as you are.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: And I may be old, but I'm not senile enough to assign a PhD in Energy Mechanics to be one of your salesmen.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: The Vice President is almost here. I doubt you have the time to fool around in my office.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Just giving you a heads-up. I'm seeing a few new investors today, and I have a number of important remote meetings to attend.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Since the Vice President is here to inspect research, I'll excuse myself.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: None of the phones in Business stopped ringing the day the Vice President announced his visit to Rhine. I had to get someone to add two dedicated hotlines.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: It's a clear signal. The world of Trimountian finance...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: No, not just Trimounts, not just finance. Every Columbian who even has a passing interest in investing has their eyes on us.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: That Bieber has a lot of stock options, doesn't he? I say you just accept his resignation, then hire him back at a lower salary when the company's stock soars and he begs for it.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Rhine Lab is not a stock market toy, Justin.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Now that is hurtful.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Mayor Benjamin, Councilman Chris, Deputy Phil, Commander Colette, even the Chief Justice... that's just a few of the people I'm talking to today.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Could Kristen have kept playing her hide-and-seek game with Blake if I hadn't continued to sweet-talk all these friends?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: You utilized a lot of resources...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Just doing my job.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: And one correction... I'm not a cornerstone of Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: A cornerstone exists for other people to build upon.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I don't have the same loyalty to Kristen as you do. I chose her and Rhine.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I helped her because I wanted to take control of my own fate, of everyone's fates.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: This isn't a game.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: News from Maylander?

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: Yes, sir. They have personnel deployed around the area to ensure your safety.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Good. How much further?

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: Two more blocks until Rhine Lab headquarters.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: Canceling today's tour is always an option, sir, if you're concerned.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: If the Maylander Foundation can't be trusted, then canceling the tour won't be enough to protect me.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I can't very well skip class to see the mining platforms chase the sun because I'm scared of exams, like I did when I was young.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Not when I'm the Vice President of the Columbia Union.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: You should get some rest while you can, sir. I doubt there will be many more chances today.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Do you remember how I described Trimounts at yesterday's banquet?

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: 'The future of Columbia.' You said you love this youthful city, just as you love this youthful nation.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: As a matter of fact, I don't like this place at all.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: There are no burdenbeasts, no clouds of dust kicked up by their hooves, no duels for some 'dumb' reason, no pioneering spirit.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Only white-collar workers and their coffee, high-rise buildings that split the sky, and... *sniff* air so clean it makes your stomach squirm.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: I believe the Trimountian circulation system employs—

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Don't, Pavard. I'll be hearing far too many explanations like that over the next few hours.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: You don't like dealing with scientists?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I won't go that far.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: They're simple. They can go on and on about their products, blueprints or ideals, sometimes outlandish, sometimes crazy, mostly incomprehensible...

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: All I need to do is smile, nod, and shake their hands when they're done, giving them a few words of encouragement.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Much simpler than dealing with the old folks of the special district.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: You represent the state. The people like to see Columbia support science. It's good for your image, and your odds in the next election.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: The vice presidential election, Columbia's biggest political event... but I'm thinking that perhaps I shouldn't spend too much time and effort on it.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: You've achieved a lot in the past several years. The polls indicate you enjoy a high level of support...

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: The representatives who support you have also been in contact with that influential Vulpo director of Rhine Lab. It's not easy to gain the support of big tech. You have a head start.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: No, I meant in comparison with Mark Max, the President ever guiding Columbia to her promised future.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: All that national attention surrounding the vice presidential elections just adds to the embarrassment.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: What is this screen showing?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: The cargo passageway behind Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: A little to the left. Zoom in... good, now there shouldn't be any dead zones.
The soldier is nervous as he operates the equipment. The Colonel has been standing behind him for some time now, his brow furrowed.
The five blocks around Rhine Lab headquarters have all been placed under surveillance.
Many figures are moving on the screens. Key areas have been blocked off, but there continues to be a considerable crowd nearby.
Of course, the crowd also provides good cover for their operations.
The soldier scans each monitor, not daring to even blink.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: What's the situation on the ground?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: All undercover and support units are in position.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Where is Ferdinand?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: He's on the phone.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: The phone?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Yes. Should I summon him?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Never mind, no need to tell him.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: What about the colleagues in the Defense Section that he talked about?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: We've 'taken over.'

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Good.
A shadow flashes across the display on the bottom-left, before appearing on the other screens. It is the Columbia displayed on top of a car.
Several black vehicles maintain equal separation with it, both in front and behind, with machine-like discipline.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Begin.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: The Vice President's convoy is in sight. Begin.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Have a nice tour, Jackson.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Mr. Vice President! There have been reports that Triton factory explosion in District 13 was linked to Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Is your visit to Rhine Lab at this time intended to dispel such speculation?

steps.name: Reporter?
steps.text: Excuse me.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: District 13 is still under lockdown. Did you authorize the army's actions, and how long will the lockdown remain in effect?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Will you be meeting with Control Wright?

steps.name: Reporter?
steps.text: Excuse me... Mr. Vice President, about your schedule in Trimounts...

steps.name: Rhine Staff
steps.text: Patience, please.

steps.name: Rhine Staff
steps.text: There will be a press conference after the Vice President has concluded his tour.

steps.name: Rhine Staff
steps.text: We have set aside a space to accommodate members of the press. Please, follow me, and refrain from disturbing other staff members in their work.

steps.name: Reporter?
steps.text: There's no one else?

steps.name: Reporter?
steps.text: Damn!

steps.name: Rhine Staff?
steps.text: Shut him up.

steps.name: Reporter?
steps.text: Mmph—

steps.name: Rhine Staff?
steps.text: Look at that, hiding weapons in recording equipment. Search him and make sure he doesn't have anything else on him.

steps.name: Rhine Staff?
steps.text: There's a discrepancy in the documents... find a way to check the credentials of all the reporters in the press area. Be discreet.

steps.name: Rhine Staff?
steps.text: I got this one. No commotion.

steps.name: Sniper
steps.text: Lost contact with A1, A2 A3...

steps.name: Sniper
steps.text: Have all our locations been compromised?!

steps.name: Sniper
steps.text: HQ, HQ, need immediate instruction on whether to continue operation—

steps.name: Sniper
steps.text: Grgh...

steps.name: Citizen?
steps.text: That's the 9th one.

steps.name: Citizen?
steps.text: If you're used to dealing with terrorists, you know a thing or two about planning a terror attack.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Report.

steps.name: Citizen?
steps.text: All potential vantage points within sniping range of Rhine Lab have been secured.

steps.name: Citizen?
steps.text: We have neutralized nine snipers and eleven disguised assassins.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Continue to monitor the area around Rhine Lab. Roads, vehicles, pedestrians... leave no stone unturned.

steps.name: Citizen?
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Citizen?
steps.text: The Vice President has entered the Rhine building. It will be difficult for us to deploy directly inside the building. Do you intend to be on scene personally?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I got a message from a colleague. There's somewhere else that I need to be.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Share intel with Dr. {@nickname} of Rhodes Island. Follow any orders issued by the Doctor.

steps.name: Citizen?
steps.text: Acknowledged.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: This one makes seven.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Just mass-produced power armor, Doctor.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Don't worry, it won't take too much effort.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: The serial numbers match the ones that the Defense Section lost, but five are still unaccounted for.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Should we keep looking? We need to eliminate them before they leave the secret passage, right?

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: They'll cause chaos if they get out, even if they can't get to the Vice President.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: How did you think of using the access permissions granted by Muelsyse to check the Defense Section's equipment log?

options: Just going down the list of possible options. I didn't expect to strike gold on the first try.
I didn't think the assassins would throw acid at the Vice President disguised as researchers.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I see.

options: Something feels off. These mechs seem cautious in their movements.
It doesn't seem so much an assassination attempt as...

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Movement, Doctor.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: No. Who could be in a secret passage at this hour...?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Doctor, Operator Rosmontis... what are you doing here?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I see... sorry, Doctor, I've been maintaining radio silence because I had infiltrated Rhine to retrieve data for Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: As for Kal'tsit's whereabouts, I have no idea either.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: The remaining power armor...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I destroyed five before running into you and the Doctor. That makes a total of twelve, which matches the number that the Defense Section lost.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And so, I went to find someone.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'm guessing the feeling of being dragged out of a suit of power armor is not something you want to experience again, Reggie.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: What orders did Ferdinand give you?

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: He only wanted to borrow a few suits of power armor.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Ferdinand can't be trusted.

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: How do I trust someone who repeatedly ignores the rules that she set, showing up at Rhine whenever she wants, who abandoned all her responsibilities?

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: He took over Defense when you left. He paid our wages for the past few years.

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: He remembers our names, our hobbies, even gives us gifts, every once in a while.

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: Ferdinand may have been an asshole.

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: But I have to say, Director Saria—

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: That asshole paid our bills.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The Vice President is still inside Rhine. You know the consequences if something happens.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: We must check everything that Ferdinand may have touched.

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: Just the ten suits of power armor. You have my word.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I destroyed seven, Saria destroyed five...

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: That's impossible!

steps.name: Defense Section Employee
steps.text: Ferdinand only borrowed ten. I watched him enter the commands myself!

options: What kind of man is Ferdinand, Saria?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Proud, arrogant, thinks himself better than everyone else.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: But if there's one thing that sets him above other people...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It's that he actually puts his boasts into action.

options: I don't think those ten mechs are for assassinating the Vice President.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: What?

options: As for the two extra ones...
Looks like he and the army are on guard against each other.
Ferdinand doesn't want the Vice President assassinated at Rhine Lab.
